$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

So claude.exe inherits our stdin read end and stdout write end by design, and any grandchild claude creates with inheritance also gets them. This is independent of job membership and of CREATE_SUSPENDED.

It needs one new windows-sys feature (Win32_System_Diagnostics_ToolHelp). The 'no thread handle' worry is answered: the handle is obtainable via Toolhelp, but std's own accessor is nightly-only.

R2 (c) harm mismatch: the stdin-inheritance gap is NOT closed by CREATE_SUSPENDED. Stdio handles must be inheritable for claude to receive them (child_pipe true), and a grandchild's inheritance is decided by claude's own CreateProcess calls, which we do not control on stable. ROADMAP's 'grandchild-inherits-stdin gap' is therefore a separate issue from the job race and needs its own decision. This is reasoning from the std source and this code, not a measured result.

R3 (c) failure path: if the suspended start succeeds but the thread lookup, OpenThread or ResumeThread fails, the child stays suspended forever, so the code must kill it. The attach_job None fallback (process.rs:58-68, 125) must still resume the child.

architect.rationale: Single-loop. The four slices have disjoint file sets (s1 commands.rs; s2 state.rs + types.ts + SessionList.tsx + App.css + new ipc.test.ts; s3 job.rs + process.rs; s4 README.md + CLAUDE.md), but a diamond is not earned: s1 is about 6 lines, s3 (as decided) is comments only, s4 is two lines, so only s2 is a real change and the whole diff is one reviewable unit (about 150 lines incl. tests). ROADMAP marks D1 as could-be-a-single-loop. Four builders, four reviewers and an integrator would cost more than the change. Risk tags: s1 low (no sensitive data, no shared file, copies the adjacent start_session/answer pattern and rustc checks it). s2 high (logic a test cannot fully see: Rust has no exhaustive match on SessionStatus so a missed transition compiles (R5); stickiness is a rule across apply/recompute/commit; a missing LIVE entry silently hides Stop on exactly the stuck session; CSS has no test). s3 low (comments only, mechanically checked that no non-comment line changed; no shared file). s4 low (prose, no sensitive data, no shared file). If the gate picks s3-alt (implement CREATE_SUSPENDED), that slice is high: unsafe Win32, a failure path that can strand a suspended child (R3), an unverified one-thread premise (U2). DECISION (b) stickiness: needs_attention is sticky until the turn ends. UnsupportedControlRequest sets it from any non-terminal status; recompute does not overwrite it (so neither a later CanUseTool nor committing an answer does); Init and Assistant do not touch it; it clears only on Result (to Idle) or stop/exit (to Ended/Failed via is_over). Justification: Result is the only message that proves claude got past the request it could not answer. Non-sticky would let a later CanUseTool set WaitingPermission, and answering it would recompute to Working, re-hiding the stuck state, which is the exact bug the ROADMAP item fixes. Pending permission/question items stay answerable (send_through rejects only Ended/Failed) and stay visible in the inbox, so stickiness hides nothing actionable. DECISION (c): do not implement CREATE_SUSPENDED; document it. The window runs from CreateProcessW returning to AssignProcessToJobObject on the same thread (microseconds), and claude.exe cannot spawn anything before its own runtime initialises. Closing it on stable needs a Toolhelp thread scan with an unverified one-thread premise (U2) and adds a stranded-suspended-child failure mode (R3): more risk added than removed. Reversal trigger: ChildExt::main_thread_handle (rust-lang/rust#96723) stabilises, giving the real thread handle with no scan. The stdin/stdout inheritance gap (R2) cannot be closed here (claude decides it in its own CreateProcess calls) and is documented only. Windows rule: every done_when runs on Windows (cargo test, npm run build, npm test, grep); none needs a Mac.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.detail: 'With a job, stop and app exit still kill it' holds only for a grandchild that is in the job. A grandchild created inside the accepted job.rs race window would escape and could still hold the pipe after stop. job.rs documents that window as not expected, so this is consistent. It is not a false claim, but the sentence could say 'a grandchild in the job'.

The window also spans Job::new (CreateJobObjectW + SetInformationJobObject) and the stdin/stdout take(), not just the AssignProcessToJobObject call. The comment's 'from CreateProcessW returning to AssignProcessToJobObject' is still accurate as stated.

s2.summary: PASS. I re-ran every done_when gate at the d1-closeout tip 72be9e3. The later commits change only comments and docs, so the s2 code is identical to b9c6ed0. cargo test gives 44 passed and 0 failed, including all 6 new tests. The greps return 5, 0, 1, 1 and 2. npm run build (tsc && vite build) exits 0, and npm test passes 3 files and 18 tests. I walked every status write and read in state.rs and mod.rs. Unsupported sets NeedsAttention, and apply() already stops at Ended/Failed. recompute() returns early on it, which covers CanUseTool and Commit::Answer (that arm is also gated on Waiting*). Init only moves Starting. Assistant leaves status alone. Result goes to Idle, and stop/exit go to Ended/Failed via finish(). Reply needs Idle, so a reply that races an unsupported request leaves NeedsAttention in place. On the frontend, LIVE is a Record with needs_attention:true. The CSS rule is in both blocks, and its contrast is within the range of the existing badges. ipc.test.ts runs the real decodeSession, with no mock needed. The stat shows only the 5 approved files (ipc.test.ts via scope_exceptions). The author is njcurtis3, with no trailers.

findings.issue: Note: an UnsupportedControlRequest that arrives while Idle (after a Result) moves the session to NeedsAttention. From there reply_line refuses with 'session is not waiting for a reply' until the next Result. claude is not mid-turn at that point, so that Result may never come, and Stop becomes the only exit. This follows the approved stickiness rule ('from any status that is not Ended/Failed'; clears only on Result or stop/exit), so it is not a defect. It is worth a sentence in the UI copy or a later decision if it shows up in practice.

Note: the epoch doc says it is 'bumped whenever status or the open requests change', but the UnsupportedControlRequest arm changes status without bumping epoch. This is harmless today. The only epoch consumer is Commit::Reply, which also requires status == Idle, so the race leaves NeedsAttention intact. The Init Starting->Working transition already does the same, so the comment was loose before this slice.

Note: the light-mode #ffc9a8 (peach) is distinct from waiting_* #ffe3a8 as required, but it is fairly close to failed #f8c9c9 (pink). Contrast is fine: about 11.6:1 light, the same as failed, and about 7.5:1 dark, between waiting (about 6.4) and failed (about 9.8). Distinguishability from failed relies on the label text. This is a taste-level observation, not a defect.
